(Fiscal Impact: $3,200,000 Expense; Fire Fund; Budgeted; Discretionary)
..body

BACKGROUND
In order to help reduce the future impacts from wildfires, the County entered into a previous Agreement (Agreement No. 210118B) with the Napa Communities Firewise Foundation (NCFF) for wildfire prevention activities. The original agreement occurred in September 2020 and was subsequently extended through five individual Amendments through December 2023. The aggregate amount for these initial Agreements was $14,166,000.  This funding has been used to provide public outreach and education on wildfire preparedness and create local Fire Safe Councils throughout the County. Also, the funding has been used to plan and execute wildfire prevention projects focused on vegetation modification and provide administrative support for these projects. 

Agreement No. 240256B was subsequently approved on January 9, 2024, providing an additional $7,000,000 to continue these wildfire prevention efforts. This funding was broken into two categories with separate Scopes of Work (SOW), as delineated in Exhibit "A" of that Agreement.  The first category totaled $6,000,000 per the County's FY 2023-24 budget appropriation in the Fire Fund. The second category for $1,000,000 was funded through an agreement with the California Department of Water Resources (DWR) for capacity building and infrastructure. The funds were received in FY 2022-23 and were then appropriated from the restricted fund balance.

An additional agreement, Agreement No. 250180B, was approved on September 10, 2024, for a total of $4,000,000 to continue these wildfire prevention efforts. The funding sources included $3,000,000 from state appropriation secured by Senator Dodd in 2023 and $1,000,000 is County general fund match. This funding provided for prevention activities that are identified in the Scope of Work (SOW) in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement subdivided into two broad categories. The first category involved continuing the work of Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP) and services and the second involved wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. The agreement was amended on November 1, 2024, to give clarity on the SOW and again on March 11, 2025, to provide an additional $123,250 of funding for additional work.

Agreement No. 260056B was approved on July 22, 2025, for a total of $3,500,000 to continue the wildfire prevention efforts. Funds are split between two major categories to continue the work of Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP) and the second involved wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement.

Staff is requesting a waiver of competitive bidding requirements and a sole source award to The Napa Communities Firewise Foundation for $3,200,000 based upon uniqueness, timeliness, and inadequate competition. Fire Administration would like to secure the vendor without securing competitive bids to maintain continuity of care of wildfire preparedness, fire safe councils, and fuels reduction projects. This is in the best interest of the County because it saves time and money by minimizing the requirements for onboarding, project development, and oversight by maintaining the continuity. NCFF has an established relationship with County communities, existing right of entry agreements, and a proven successful model for supporting Firewise Communities, implementing Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP), and managing large scale vegetation treatment projects .

This funding of $3,200,000 provides for prevention activities that are identified in the Scope of Work (SOW) in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. These activities are subdivided into two broad categories. The first category will involve continuing the work of the CWPP and services. This will involve providing community-based wildland fire awareness programs. The programs will provide Napa County residents in high-risk communities with the knowledge they need to survive wildfires. It will also provide public outreach via workshops, newsletters, and literature to educate Napa County residents. In addition, the funding will provide outreach and support to new communities interested in forming a Fire Safety Council to manage and protect a given geographic area within Napa County. This support shall be ongoing for all councils for the life of the contract. The second category of wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. These projects are located throughout the entire county and include roadside clearances, creating more viable access and egress routes in the event of a wildfire, fuel breaks in strategic locations, and grazing projects to reduce overall fuel loads in specified locations.  

Some projects have had environmental reviews and have completed permitting, while some are in the process of being completed. There is also a list of proposed projects that are scheduled for environmental review via the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).  The various proposed activities are either categorically exempt from CEQA as minor alterations to land for fuel management activities pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15304, categorically exempt from CEQA as information collection and resource evaluation pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15306, or are not a project as defined by CEQA Guidelines section 15378 and, therefore, CEQA is not applicable.

Exhibit "B" outlines the plan for compensation and expense reimbursements for this Agreement.  The majority of the $3,200,000 is dedicated to fuel mitigation programs, while the remaining amount will be used for environmental compliance, wildfire preparedness programs, grant writing and funding strategy services, program and project personnel, and some indirect costs to administering this funding source.  

This Agreement is an important component of the County's long-term planning for a more fire resilient future.

..body

BACKGROUND
Axon Enterprise, Inc. (Axon), an Arizona corporation, provides Justice Premier, a cloud-based Digital Evidence Management System (DEMS) that enables the secure receipt, storage, and sharing of discovery and other case related items for criminal cases. Through this system, law enforcement agencies submit digital evidence directly to the District Attorney's Office who then provides discovery to the defense.

In April 2023, Napa County Information Technology Services entered into an agreement with Axon on behalf of the District Attorney's Office to streamline and centralize digital evidence storage using Axon's Evidence.com platform. The Napa County Sheriff's Office also utilizes Axon services, and Axon remains the only solution that provides countywide access to digital evidence uploaded by county law enforcement agencies. Based on this exclusivity and Axon's existing contracts with county law enforcement partners, Axon qualifies as a sole source provider.

The Axon Justice Premier software offers several enhanced features that will provide the Public Defender's Office with the same access that the District Attorney's Office's has concerning digital evidence, including:
  -  Pro licenses for all Department staff (currently limited in number)
  -  Multi-camera video playback
  -  Axon transcription assistant tools
  -  Ability to play third-party video formats directly from Evidence.com
  -  Automated redaction tools
  -  Axon Citizen, enabling staff to receive files directly through a secure upload link
  -  Advanced discovery tools supporting full Brady disclosure compliance
  -  Unlimited secure cloud storage for attorneys and investigators

Six law enforcement agencies in Napa County and the District Attorney's Office currently use Axon.  Adoption of Axon Justice Premier by the Public Defender's Office will permit the same access to discovery and digital files that the District Attorney's Office currently has which will significantly reduce time previously required to deliver and access evidence through paper reports, files, flash drives, CDs, DVDs, and email.

Justice Premier provides standardized file formats, tools to trim audio and video for efficient review, time-stamped metrics, tagging for relevant incident segments, and automated redaction of faces and license plates. The system can also generate transcriptions of interviews, 911 calls, and jail calls, and includes tools to improve audio and image clarity. Unlimited cloud storage ensures long-term retention of case files and consistent access even as attorney assignments change.  Justice Premier maintains a complete chain of custody from the time evidence is received, reducing risks related to misplaced evidence, or undocumented edits. Original file formats remain intact, with all enhancements performed on copies.

Axon meets all FBI Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) and California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System security requirements, including U.S. based storage, controlled access, and protections against data breaches. The system provides 24/7 technical support, controlled evidence access, and the ability to recover deleted files within seven days. It supports most standard file types without requiring proprietary formats, offering reliable, secure digital evidence infrastructure for the County.

This agreement is for ten-years with annual cost increases. The first year the agreement will cost approximately $52,558.00.

     2.  Approve a waiver of competitive bidding and sole source award to Axon Enterprises Inc. of Scottsdale, Arizona.

The funding sources included $3,000,000 from state appropriation secured by Senator Dodd in 2023 and $1,000,000 is County general fund match. This funding provided for prevention activities that are identified in the Scope of Work (SOW) in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement subdivided into two broad categories. The first category involved continuing the work of Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP) and services and the second involved wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. The agreement was amended on November 1, 2024, to give clarity on the SOW and again on March 11, 2025, to provide an additional $123,250 of funding for additional work.

Agreement No. 260056B was approved on July 22, 2025, for a total of $3,500,000 to continue the wildfire prevention efforts. Funds are split between two major categories to continue the work of Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP) and the second involved wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement.

Staff is requesting a waiver of competitive bidding requirements and a sole source award to The Napa Communities Firewise Foundation for $3,200,000 based upon uniqueness, timeliness, and inadequate competition. Fire Administration would like to secure the vendor without securing competitive bids to maintain continuity of care of wildfire preparedness, fire safe councils, and fuels reduction projects. This is in the best interest of the County because it saves time and money by minimizing the requirements for onboarding, project development, and oversight by maintaining the continuity. NCFF has an established relationship with County communities, existing right of entry agreements, and a proven successful model for supporting Firewise Communities, implementing Napa County's Community Wildfire Protection Plan (CWPP), and managing large scale vegetation treatment projects. This sole source request is in compliance with the recommendations in the most recent contract audit.

This funding of $3,200,000 provides for prevention activities that are identified in the Scope of Work (SOW) in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. These activities are subdivided into two broad categories. The first category will involve continuing the work of the CWPP and services. This will involve providing community-based wildland fire awareness programs. The programs will provide Napa County residents in high-risk communities with the knowledge they need to survive wildfires. It will also provide public outreach via workshops, newsletters, and literature to educate Napa County residents. In addition, the funding will provide outreach and support to new communities interested in forming a Fire Safety Council to manage and protect a given geographic area within Napa County. This support shall be ongoing for all councils for the life of the contract. The second category of wildfire prevention efforts will involve performing planned vegetation treatment projects that are also identified in the SOW in Exhibit "A" of the Agreement. These projects are located throughout the entire county and include roadside clearances, creating more viable access and egress routes in the event of a wildfire, fuel breaks in strategic locations, and grazing projects to reduce overall fuel loads in specified locations.  

Some projects have had environmental reviews and have completed permitting, while some are in the process of being completed. There is also a list of proposed projects that are scheduled for environmental review via the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).  The various proposed activities are either categorically exempt from CEQA as minor alterations to land for fuel management activities pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15304, categorically exempt from CEQA as information collection and resource evaluation pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15306, or are not a project as defined by CEQA Guidelines section 15378 and, therefore, CEQA is not applicable.

Exhibit "B" outlines the plan for compensation and expense reimbursements for this Agreement.  The majority of the $3,200,000 is dedicated to fuel mitigation programs, while the remaining amount will be used for environmental compliance, wildfire preparedness programs, grant writing and funding strategy services, program and project personnel, and some indirect costs to administering this funding source.  

This Agreement is an important component of the County's long-term planning for a more fire resilient future.

BACKGROUND
The funding source of revenue: Under the California Digital Infrastructure and Video Competition Act (DIVCA) of 2006, local franchising authorities can require state video franchise holders (such as cable and certain broadband providers) to pay a PEG fee of 1% of their gross revenues derived within that jurisdiction. PEG funds are strictly used to support local community media facilities. This includes purchasing broadcast equipment, upgrading studio hardware, and maintaining production gear for local public access, school, and government meetings programming.
On September 12, 2023, the Board approved the use of Public, Educational, and Governmental (PEG) funds and established the CIP and funding needed to implement upgrades to County media capacity in the Board Chambers. This was phase one of an AV project which was intended to create a modern, integrated, user-friendly system that would reduce technical disruptions and make the Board Chambers easier for County staff to operate.
Phase one was the larger, comprehensive modernization of the Board Chambers. It addressed the room's outdated AV infrastructure and operational problems, including cameras, monitors/displays, microphones/audio, equipment locations, staff workstations, and the integration of the technology needed for in-person, remote, and broadcast meetings. The number and placement of monitors were improved to provide a more open and functional meeting space. New cameras were installed in locations designed to provide a more professional video feed. Individual monitors were provided at each dais position to allow Board and Commission members to easily view meeting information. These improvements are complete and establish the foundation of the updated Board Chambers AV environment.
Completing phase two has become increasingly important as California strengthens its requirements for public access to local government meetings. Senate Bill 707 (SB 707) expands upon provisions related to teleconferencing and public participation under the Ralph M. Brown Act by highlighting the need for dependable technology and systems that enable community members to access and participate in public meetings remotely and through electronic platforms.
The County relies on electronic and remote access to public meetings. An interruption in the AV system can affect more than the meeting experience for staff and Board members. A failure of critical AV equipment can interrupt or degrade the County’s ability to provide the public with a reliable means of viewing and participating in a meeting. This is particularly important when members of the public rely on remote access rather than attending meetings in person.
  
The second phase of the project includes replacement of aging and failing AV components, as well as reorganization of the existing new equipment into an appropriately configured AV equipment rack. The current rack configuration has evolved over time as equipment has been added or replaced, making maintenance, troubleshooting, and future upgrades increasingly difficult. Rebuilding the system into a properly organized rack will improve cable management, accessibility, airflow, serviceability, and overall system reliability while reducing potential points of failure.

The proposed equipment was selected based on compatibility with the County’s existing AV environment and the operational requirements of the Board Chambers.  Standardizing equipment will improve system performance and reliability, simplify ongoing maintenance and troubleshooting, and provide appropriate manufacturer support for the equipment moving forward.

Staff have experienced an increasing number of equipment failures due to the age and condition of the existing system, requiring troubleshooting and temporary workarounds to maintain meeting operations.  As the equipment continues to age, the likelihood of a failure affecting a public meeting or broadcast increases.  Replacing these critical components reduces that risk and provides a more reliable and supportable AV environment for Board meetings and other public meetings conducted in the Chambers.  The total equipment cost is $35,000.

PCD is Crestron-certified and is an authorized dealer for much of the equipment currently used within the Board Chambers, allowing the vendor to provide both the specialized programming services and manufacturer-supported hardware necessary for the project.

The County no longer has an active support agreement with its previous AV vendor, leaving the Board Chambers without dedicated vendor support for its specialized AV infrastructure. Establishing a relationship with PCD through this project will provide access to qualified technical support for the existing system and the equipment being installed. Because certain hardware repairs, replacements, programming, and commissioning activities must be performed through an authorized or certified provider, qualified vendor support remains necessary even if County staff expand their internal Crestron expertise in the future.

Using PCD for the replacement, integration, programming, and commissioning of the equipment will provide continuity between the County's existing Crestron environment and the upgraded system while ensuring the equipment is installed and supported by a vendor with the required certifications and manufacturer relationships.  The total cost for one-year support is $4,800.

PCD is the only local certified vendor identified by the County who can program, support, and commission the County's existing Crestron-based AV systems. 

Requested Actions:
1. Authorize the purchase of Audiovisual equipment with one-year support; and 
2. Establish equipment as a capital asset in the amount of $39,800; and
3. Approve a waiver of competitive bidding requirements and sole source award for the purchase of Audiovisual equipment and support from PCD.

FISCAL IMPACT
Is there a Fiscal Impact?
	Yes		Is it currently budgeted?	Yes		Where is it budgeted?	Fund 4200, Subdivision 4200020 Public Television Educational and Governmental Funds (PEG)	
	Is it Mandatory or Discretionary?	Discretionary		Discretionary Justification:	New equipment is necessary to maintain reliable audiovisual operations for Board meetings and public broadcasts, reducing equipment failures and ensuring continuity of service.		Is the general fund affected?	No		Future fiscal impact:	The replacement equipment is expected to reduce maintenance requirements and emergency repairs. Ongoing costs will be limited to standard maintenance and any applicable manufacturer support or warranty renewals.	
	Consequences if not approved:	If this purchase is not approved, the County will continue to rely on aging, failure-prone equipment, increasing the likelihood of meeting disruptions, broadcast interruptions, and emergency repairs that could negatively impact public access and Board operations.
